english_explanation: Multipart form field names were escaped for double quotes only (val.replace("\"", "%22")), leaving CR/LF untouched, so a field or file name containing a newline was written raw into the Content-Disposition header line. KeyVal#contentType(String) had the same shape, accepting a content-type with embedded CR/LF and validating nothing. Together these allow CRLF injection into the serialized multipart request.
exact_path: ROUTE 1: HttpConnection#encodeMimeName(String) [ENTRY + FAULT, old lines 119-121] || ROUTE 2: HttpConnection$KeyVal#contentType(String) [ENTRY + FAULT]

english_explanation: Element#appendChild accepted an element as its own child with no cycle check, making it simultaneously its own parent and child. Any later traversal or serialization walked the cycle forever, including the test framework's own failure reporting. Reporter's whole repro was two lines: Element e = new Element(Tag.valueOf("div"), ""); e.appendChild(e);

A regression from jsoup 1.21.2 (change for #2355) made NodeTraversor re-enter head() on whatever node occupied the current sibling position after replaceWith(), before()+remove(), or after()+remove(). Calling replaceWith() inside a visitor's head() therefore looped indefinitely. Maintainer confirmed and refactored the traversal into a forward-cursor walk.
fault_site: NodeTraversor#traverse(NodeVisitor,Node) - same method as entry point

english_explanation: XmlTreeBuilder overrode defaultMaxDepth() to return Integer.MAX_VALUE, while the HTML tree builder uses TreeBuilder's bounded default of 512. Deeply nested XML therefore grew the stack without limit until the JVM failed. The fix removes the override entirely.
fault_site: XmlTreeBuilder#defaultMaxDepth (old lines 104-108) and Parser#xmlParser calling setMaxDepth(Integer.MAX_VALUE)

english_explanation: Attributes#checkNotNull cast any non-null attribute value straight to String (return val == null ? EmptyString : (String) val), but the class's own userData() method stores a Map<String,Object> in an internal attribute slot. Any read path over an element carrying user data threw ClassCastException.

english_explanation: Attribute.getValidKey() returns null for a name that cannot legally start an XML name, such as "1abc". The attribute-setting caller null-checked that return; the element-name caller in W3CBuilder#head did not, and dereferenced it via tagName.contains(":"), throwing NullPointerException during W3CDom conversion.

english_explanation: For inputs small enough to be fully consumed inside the 5 KB charset-sniff read-ahead, DataUtil's charset detection read and closed the entire input - a valid optimization for parse(), which can reuse the fully sniffed Document. But streamParser() still needs a live readable input afterward, and Validate.notNull(input) then threw ValidationException: Object must not be null.
fault_site: DataUtil#detectCharset - closes/consumes the input it was only meant to sniff

english_explanation: During charset sniffing jsoup called InputStream.available() purely as a speed hint. On JDK 8's legacy HttpURLConnection, available() throws IOException: Stream closed once the peer closes the socket, and the unguarded call aborted the whole parse. Reporter found it chasing a flaky ConnectTest.maxBodySize failure on JDK 8 Ubuntu CI; in their words the exception 'was too strong a signal'. Fix wraps both call sites in try/catch.

english_explanation: Re2jRegex$Re2jMatcher#find caught only StackOverflowError around the delegate re2j matcher's find(), wrapping it into ValidationException(PatternComplexityError); other allocation failures from the regex engine escaped unnormalized. The fix broadens the catch so allocation errors are normalized consistently.

W3CDom.fromJsoup dropped XML processing instructions and any comment outside the root element, and converted CDataNode instances into ordinary text nodes. Silent, observable data loss during DOM conversion - no exception and no warning; the caller simply received less document than they supplied.
fault_site: W3CDom$W3CBuilder#head - intra-method instanceof dispatch chain with no branch for PI, document-level comment, or CDATA

english_explanation: Template end-tag and EOF processing did not distinguish elements created from input from the synthetic context element that fragment parsing pushes. HtmlTreeBuilder#onStack(String) matched that context element by tag name, so in a fragment parse whose context element is itself named "template", onStack("template") returned true with no matching entry ever pushed onto the separate template-mode stack. Code guarded by that check then popped a mode that was never there, and resetInsertionMode's guard fired.

english_explanation: The Cleaner compared attribute keys case-insensitively when deciding admission but wrote them under the raw preserved-case key, while the enforced attribute was written under the canonical lower-case key. The two never collided, so the enforced attribute was appended alongside the source one instead of replacing it. Parsing One with preserveCase and cleaning with an enforced rel produced One. Reporter noted the same duplication with the standard Safelist.basic() nofollow handling.

english_explanation: Tokenizer tag names were normalized with trim(), so a name ending in a control character could take on the parsing behaviour of a different element. Parsing '<template\u001e><select><input>', every literal name.equals("template") check in the state machine failed to match and the tag fell through five insertion modes before InBody's generic fallback inserted it as an ordinary element - exposing raw data as markup on serialization. Fix lower-cases source names without trimming, retaining trim for programmatic Tag.valueOf input.

english_explanation: Supplementary (astral) code points were tested for encodability on their low 16 bits only. appendEscaped passed a truncated char where the full int code point was needed, so under a non-UTF, non-ASCII charset such as ISO-8859-1, U+100A3 was tested as if it were U+00A3 - the pound sign, which encodes fine - and the character was emitted unchanged instead of being escaped. Fix checks complete code points while preserving the ASCII and UTF fast paths.

exact_path: Entities#escape(String,Document$OutputSettings) [ENTRY] -> Entities#escapeString -> Entities#doEscape -> Entities#appendEscaped [truncating call site, old line 273] -> Entities#canEncode(CoreCharset,char,CharsetEncoder) [FAULT, old line 350]

english_explanation: containsIgnoreCase built two uniformly-cased copies of the target (all-lower and all-upper) and searched for each with an exact case-sensitive scan, so a genuinely mixed-case sequence such as '' matched neither. RCDATA elements therefore missed mixed-case end tags when tag-shaped text preceded them: <p>Foo created a real body p element instead of keeping the text as title, and created an actual img element.
fault_site: StringUtil#containsIgnoreCase / CharacterReader#containsIgnoreCase - two uniform-case copies vs a case-sensitive scan

english_explanation: The redirect handler unconditionally forced the next request to GET and dropped data, body and Content-Type for every status except 307, violating RFC 9110: 301 and 302 must preserve methods other than POST, 303 must preserve HEAD, and 307/308 must preserve the method entirely. Multipart boundaries were also lost across redirects. Fix extracts the decision into a new static helper redirectMethod(int,Method) and fails safely when a streamed body cannot be replayed.

HTTP media type names are case-insensitive, but jsoup matched them case-sensitively and rejected responses such as 'Text/HTML; charset=UTF-8'. The same regex - Pattern.compile("(\\w+)/\\w*\\+?xml.*") with no CASE_INSENSITIVE flag and an unanchored trailing .* - also rejected structured media types carrying registered subtype characters like application/vnd.example+xml, while incorrectly treating application/notxml and application/xmlish as XML.
fault_site: HttpConnection$Response#execute, old lines 852-855 (xmlContentTypeRxp field) and 962-974 (text/xml accept-reject branching)

english_explanation: StringUtil.resolve built new URL(protocol, host, port, file) with no host validation, so an http(s) URL with an empty host survived resolution, contrary to RFC 9110's authority requirement for those schemes. Downstream, Safelist's protocol validation works on the string form, so a hostless value such as https:/foo/bar satisfied a string-prefix check for an allowed protocol and was revived by the Cleaner instead of being rejected. Fix inserts validateHttpUrl(resolved) immediately after resolution.
fault_site: StringUtil#resolve(URL,String) - no host validation before returning

english_explanation: HttpConnection.KeyVal#inputStream(InputStream) read Validate.notNullParam(value, "inputStream") - validating the KeyVal's already-set string field 'value' (typically a filename such as "thumb.jpg") instead of the inputStream parameter actually passed in. Because value is normally non-null, the documented null-check on the argument never fired. One line, one wrong identifier, and the guard silently did nothing.
fault_site: HttpConnection$KeyVal#inputStream, old line 1437 - validates 'value' field instead of the 'inputStream' parameter
